audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows were off. Level 2 read Irelia while whys[1] ends 'it's even on reaction'; Levels 4-5 read Skill while whys[3] describes her repeating reset-trades faster than Sap Magic heals; 2+ items read Irelia while whys[6] and spikes[3] both say Maokai reclaims value as a tank.
audit.why: The lane's real arc is even at 1-2, Irelia's from 3 through first item once Bladesurge charges and Flawless Duet are online, and Maokai's at two items when the fight stops being a duel. The packet chart says exactly that and the mirror audit flipped these same three rows on its side.
audit.corrected: Level 2 to Skill, Levels 4-5 to Irelia at 3/10, 2+ items to Maokai at 7/10 — matched full+content pairs, one atomic group. Ratings are the inverse of the mirror's 7/10 and 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3].why and phases[6].why were boilerplate naming no spike, on the two rows that just changed hands.
audit.why: The 4-5 spike is her reset tempo — a 13s Flawless Duet against an 11s Twisted Advance — and the two-item spike is Maokai stopping being a duellist at all.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten with those numbers and the resulting instruction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says in three places that Defiant Dance 'eats your Q burst' (whys[3], spikes[2].text, mid). Riot's text: 'She takes reduced PHYSICAL damage during the charge.' Bramble Smash deals magic damage. Defiant Dance does not reduce it at all.
audit.why: This is the load-bearing error on the page. A Maokai who believes his Q is wasted into a charging Irelia will hold it and give up his only reliable damage in the trade — when in fact the Q lands in full and the charge only blunts his autos. What actually beats him at 4-5 is her reset tempo, not her damage reduction.
audit.corrected: Corrected in whys[3], spikes[2].text and mid, each stating that the reduction is physical-only and re-attributing the 4-5 loss to reset tempo.
sources: ownerKit Q text: deals magic damage

audit.whatIsWrong: late says 'her passive shreds your stacked resistances'. Ionian Fervor is stacking bonus attack speed, with bonus on-hit damage at maximum stacks — no shred of any kind.
audit.why: Resistances are the entire Maokai build plan. Telling him they are shredded points him away from the items that actually work in the matchup.
audit.corrected: late and spikes[2].text rewritten to attack-speed stacking. The mirror audit replaced the same 'shred' claim on its side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said Twisted Advance is untargetable in flight.
audit.why: It is the counter to the ability the whole page is built around tracking: an Irelia who throws Flawless Duet or Bladesurge into the dash loses the entire commit. The page instead tells the player to wait out a 16-second cooldown.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Flawless Duet's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Hers: stacked Bladesurge charges and a 13s Flawless Duet let her trade and reset out before your 11s W returns. Farm and wait.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Irelia carry threat 9/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on you take it back as a team piece — R starts the fight and W peels her off a carry she would otherwise delete.

edits.before: - Irelia Flawless Duet: matchup-defining — Her engage CC. Root/dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Irelia Flawless Duet: matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1, 850 range, and the blades must converge on you. Commit after it. - Bladesurge is 15 mana and refreshes on a marked or dying target — deny the resets.

edits.before: W-root Irelia the moment his answer is down, Q-knockback the follow-up, and let brush saplings tax his every path.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is untargetable in flight — W her as she casts and the stun whiffs. Then Q her back and sapling her path.

edits.before: Her W (Defiant Dance) eats your Q burst and she repeats reset-trades faster than Sap Magic heals them.
edits.after: Defiant Dance cuts only physical damage, so my magic Q lands — but she reset-trades faster than Sap Magic heals.

edits.before: Her first completed item (Trinity / Blade) lets her W (Defiant Dance) eat your Q burst and out-DPS your Sap Magic sustain.
edits.after: Her first item (Trinity / Blade) plus stacked Ionian Fervor attack speed out-DPSes Sap Magic, and Defiant Dance blunts your autos.

edits.before: This is where she edges ahead. Once Irelia has stacked Q (Bladesurge) charges and her E (Flawless Duet) stun, she dashes in, trades, and resets out before your W is back — and her W (Defiant Dance) eats your Q burst if she times it. Save W to punish her AFTER she commits a Q, not to start the fight, and keep saplings between you so she can't freely engage. At 6 your R (Nature's Grasp) adds gank and all-in threat, but it barely moves the 1v1, so use it to set up your jungler rather than to solo her.
edits.after: This is where she edges ahead. Once Irelia has stacked Q (Bladesurge) charges and her E (Flawless Duet) stun on 13s, she dashes in, trades, and resets out before your W is back. Defiant Dance only reduces PHYSICAL damage, so it never blunts Bramble Smash — your magic burst lands through the charge, and what actually beats you is her reset tempo. Save W to punish after she commits a Q, and keep saplings between you. At 6 your R adds gank threat but barely moves the 1v1.

edits.before: Late, accept that the straight 1v1 belongs to her — a fed Irelia kites your slow melee and her passive shreds your stacked resistances. But this is your phase as a team piece: your R (Nature's Grasp) wall and W root chain start fights your carries finish, and you peel her off them better than she can ever solo you. Don't try to win the splitpush duel; group, save W for her dash-in, and let your teamfight utility outscale her single-target snowball.
edits.after: Late, accept that the straight 1v1 belongs to her — a fed Irelia kites your slow melee and Ionian Fervor stacks attack speed until she out-DPSes your healing. But this is your phase as a team piece: your R (Nature's Grasp) wall and W root chain start fights your carries finish, and you peel her off them better than she can ever solo you. Don't try to win the splitpush duel; group, save W for her dash-in, and let your utility outscale her snowball.

notes: The Defiant Dance correction is the one to look at first: 'her W eats your Q burst' appeared in whys[3], spikes[2] and mid, and it is simply false — Bramble Smash is magic damage and Defiant Dance reduces physical only. I re-attributed the 4-5 loss to her reset tempo, which the same paragraphs already described accurately. tradeGood is duplicated verbatim into dosFull[1].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t; I rewrote only tradeGood, so those three still carry the old 'his answer' wording and will read inconsistently until someone does a sweep. Maokai's Q keeps a derived 'grounding' flag Riot's text does not support, so I made no claim that Bramble Smash stops Bladesurge — which would be a very big deal in this matchup if true.
